_meanings:
A king of the Sindhu district and brother-in-law of Duryodhana,
 having married Duhśalā, daughter of Dhṛtarāṣṭra. [Once while out
 on hunting, he chanced to see Draupadī in the forest, and asked of her
 food for himself and his retinue. Draupadī, by virtue of her magical
 sthālī, was able to supply him with materials sufficient for their break-fast.
 Jayadratha was so much struck with this act, as well as her personal charms,
 that he asked her to elope with him. She, of course, indignantly refused,
 but he succeeded in carrying her off, as her husbands were out on hunting.
 When they returned they pursued and captured the ravisher and released
 Draupadī; and he himself was allowed to go after having been subjected
 to many humiliations. He took a leading part in compassing the death of
 Abhimanyu, and met his doom at the hands of Arjuna in the great war.]
